result.policy:
PayGuard deployment policy (fixed; the audit may not change it)
- One global decision threshold applies to both channels. A transaction is flagged
  for manual review when risk_score >= threshold.
- R1: Flagged transactions must cover at least 85% of the
  labeled fraud value across all channels.
- R2: Flagged transactions must cover at least 70% of the
  labeled fraud value within each channel (Website and Mobile App separately).
- R3: No more than 200 transactions may be flagged on any single UTC
  calendar day. This is a maximum per day, not an average.
- Fraud-value recall = value of labeled fraud that is flagged / total value of labeled fraud.
  Flagging a transaction does not mean the fraud was stopped or the money recovered.
- Precision, transaction-level recall, false positives, and average precision are
  diagnostics only. They are not requirements.
Permitted changes the audit may recommend (each needs explicit human approval):
- A higher daily review capacity, up to 260 transactions per day,
  with one global threshold.
- Separate thresholds for Website and Mobile App with the original daily capacity.
- The two changes may not be combined.
Preference: a compliant option that needs no extra review capacity is preferred. If none
exists, the smallest verified capacity increase within the permitted range is preferred.
result.holdout: A later holdout window exists. It is sealed, and no tool can read it.

medium.investigation_summary:
Deployment Audit Summary — PayGuard Fraud Classifier

1. Deployment Decision Under the Original Policy
The classifier CANNOT be deployed under the original deployment policy (one global threshold, daily review capacity of 200 flagged transactions per UTC day). Neither the current configuration nor any other single global threshold satisfies all four requirements on the 28-day validation window (2026-08-03 to 2026-08-30; 133,285 transactions).

2. Evaluation of Current Configuration (Global Threshold = 0.50, Daily Capacity = 200)
- R1 (Overall fraud-value recall >= 85%): FAIL — 64.03% (0.6403).
- R2 Website (Website fraud-value recall >= 70%): PASS — 91.29% (0.9129; $258,184.18 of $282,823.53).
- R2 Mobile App (Mobile App fraud-value recall >= 70%): FAIL — 20.07% (0.2007; $35,199.28 of $175,404.53).
- R3 (Busiest single UTC day <= 200 flags): PASS — max 85 flags on 2026-08-13 (mean 66.9, min 43; 1,874 total flags).
(Diagnostics only: precision 0.8378, transaction recall 0.5493. Per policy, flagging sends a transaction to manual review and does not mean fraud was stopped or money recovered.)

3. Conflicting Requirements Under a Single Global Threshold
Across the 0.001 risk-score grid on the validation window, the requirement boundaries are:
- R1 (>= 85% overall fraud-value recall) requires threshold <= 0.137 (85.13% at 0.137 vs. 84.89% at 0.138).
- R2 Website (>= 70% Website fraud-value recall) holds across the entire candidate range (e.g., 98.23% at 0.108, 91.29% at 0.50, and 76.87% even at 0.85).
- R2 Mobile App (>= 70% Mobile App fraud-value recall) requires threshold <= 0.108 (70.08% at 0.108 vs. 69.96% at 0.109).
- R3 (<= 200 flags on the busiest single UTC day) requires threshold >= 0.118 (max 200 flags on 2026-08-29 at 0.118 vs. max 201 flags on 2026-08-29 at 0.117).

Conflict: R2 for Mobile App (threshold <= 0.108) and R3 (threshold >= 0.118) directly conflict. Note that R1 and R3 do not conflict on their own (thresholds 0.118 to 0.137 satisfy R1, R2 Website, and R3, with Mobile App fraud-value recall between 65.24% and 68.29%). Lowering the global threshold to 0.108 to reach 70.08% Mobile App fraud-value recall pushes peak single-day volume to 205 flags on 2026-08-29 (violating R3, even though the daily mean is 168.5), while raising the global threshold to 0.118 to cap peak daily flags at 200 reduces Mobile App fraud-value recall to 68.29% (violating R2 Mobile App).

4. Investigation of Permitted Policy Changes & Recommendation
Both permitted policy changes (which cannot be combined and each require explicit human approval) were tested on the validation window:

- Option A — Separate Channel Thresholds with Original Capacity of 200/day (RECOMMENDED):
  Per the policy's preference rule, a compliant option requiring no extra review capacity is preferred over increasing daily capacity. Separate channel thresholds resolve the conflict because Website maintains >94% fraud-value recall at higher thresholds while shedding false-positive volume, freeing daily review capacity for a lower Mobile App threshold.
  Recommended tested configuration: website_threshold = 0.30, mobile_app_threshold = 0.10 (daily_capacity = 200):
  - R1 (Overall fraud-value recall >= 85%): PASS — 86.21% (0.8621).
  - R2 Website (>= 70%): PASS — 94.52% (0.9452; $267,322.42 / $282,823.53).
  - R2 Mobile App (>= 70%): PASS — 72.82% (0.7282; $127,735.43 / $175,404.53).
  - R3 (Max single-day flags <= 200): PASS — max 191 flags on 2026-08-29 (mean 158.0, min 133; 4,425 total flags).
  - Diagnostics: precision 0.4820, transaction recall 0.7463 (2,133 true positives, 2,292 false positives).
  (Alternative verified zero-capacity pairs include website_threshold = 0.35, mobile_app_threshold = 0.10 with R1 86.01%, Website 94.18%, Mobile App 72.82%, max daily flags 189; and website_threshold = 0.30, mobile_app_threshold = 0.108 with R1 85.16%, Website 94.52%, Mobile App 70.08%, max daily flags 185. Using 0.30 / 0.10 provides healthier margin above R1 and R2 Mobile App while staying 9 flags below the R3 cap.)

- Option B — Daily Capacity Increase with One Global Threshold (Not Preferred):
  Under a single global threshold, the smallest verified compliant capacity increase on the validation window is daily_capacity = 205 at threshold = 0.108 (R1: 87.45%, R2 Website: 98.23%, R2 Mobile App: 70.08%, R3 max daily flags: 205 on 2026-08-29, mean 168.5; diagnostics: precision 0.4693, transaction recall 0.7747). Because Option A achieves compliance with zero extra review capacity, Option A is preferred under policy rules.

5. Limitations / Inconclusive Evidence
Compliance on the sealed holdout window and future live traffic is inconclusive from validation data alone, as no tool can inspect the holdout window and daily peak flag counts or channel fraud-value distributions may shift over time. Explicit human approval is required before adopting the recommended channel-threshold policy change.
